summary: An announcement that SRI-ARC produced a Quick Reference Card for TNLS, the terminal version of NLS. It covers basic commands, TIP settings for reaching SRI-ARC, basic TENEX commands, and view specification codes. A copy would go to each station agent, with more on request.

plainLanguage.summary: A cheat sheet card for a computer program, with its most used commands, was made and mailed out.

subtitle: A quick reference card for TNLS terminal commands and settings is now available.

tldr.problem: Users of TNLS (the terminal version of the Online System) needed a convenient reference for everyday commands, special features, and configuration.
tldr.mechanism: SRI-ARC created a quick reference card documenting basic TNLS commands, settings for connecting via TIP (Terminal Interface Protocol), basic TENEX/EXECUTIVE commands, and a complete set of VIEWSPECS codes for controlling display output.
tldr.outcome: Each network site received a card, with additional copies available on request, making it easier for TNLS users to work without constantly consulting documentation.

today: RFC 496 is a historical announcement of a printed aid for a 1973 network system. Such reference cards were common before digital documentation and help systems became ubiquitous.

sections.title: The Reference Card
sections.content: RFC 496 announces the TNLS Quick Reference Card, a portable guide for users of the terminal-based Online System. The card documents all basic commands needed for everyday work and special-purpose features. It includes TIP settings for reaching SRI-ARC over the network, basic TENEX/EXECUTIVE operating system commands, and a comprehensive set of VIEWSPECS codes.
sections.plainLanguage: A quick card was made with the most common commands people needed to use a network program.

sections.title: VIEWSPECS and Display Control
sections.content: VIEWSPECS are codes that control how the Online System displays information on the terminal screen. These codes let users customize the appearance of output and are crucial to effective use of NLS. TNLS users depend on viewspec codes to format data the way they need it for different tasks and preferences.
sections.plainLanguage: Special codes let you change how text looked on your terminal screen, so you could see information the way you wanted.

sections.title: Distribution and Availability
sections.content: The quick reference card was distributed to all network sites through their station agents. Each site received one copy initially, with additional copies available on request from Marcia Keeney at SRI-ARC. Users could request as many copies as needed for their site. The card was designed to fit in a pocket or be posted at a terminal for quick lookup during work.
sections.plainLanguage: Everyone got one card in the mail, and more were available if they asked for them.
